about: Standalone studies (dist/studies/<id>.html) plus the sources and styles they introduce. Merged by scripts/generate-catalog.mjs. Checked 18 November 2026 against official sites and GitHub repositories.

sources.name: View Transitions API
sources.license: Web platform feature; no licence needed
sources.bestFor: List-to-detail morphs and page transitions without a library
sources.caveat: Same-document transitions are Baseline since October 2025; cross-document transitions are Chromium and Safari 18.2+ only.

sources.name: CSS scroll-driven animations
sources.license: Web platform feature; no licence needed
sources.bestFor: Reading progress, reveals and parallax without scroll listeners
sources.caveat: Chromium and Safari 26; check Firefox before relying on it. Always wrap in @supports.

sources.name: liquid-glass (nikdelvin)
sources.bestFor: Apple Liquid Glass-style refraction with no WebGL
sources.caveat: backdrop-filter:url() refracts in Chromium; Safari falls back to blur. For WebGL refraction see liquidGL.
sources.install: Copy the SVG filter and CSS

sources.name: M3E (Material 3 Expressive web components)
sources.license: MIT; community project, not affiliated with Google
sources.bestFor: Material 3 Expressive shapes, motion and components on the web
sources.caveat: Google has no official Expressive web library; Material trademarks belong to Google.

sources.name: Fancy Components
sources.bestFor: Playful text effects and micro-interactions
sources.caveat: React only; copy components individually.

sources.name: fffuel
sources.license: Free tools; check the site's terms for each asset
sources.bestFor: Grain, gradients, blobs, patterns and textures as SVG
sources.caveat: Hosted tools, no code library.
sources.install: Use in the browser and export SVG

sources.name: Adobe Leonardo
sources.bestFor: Contrast-first, accessible colour scales and themes
sources.caveat: Targets WCAG 2 contrast; check APCA separately if you use it.

sources.name: Rive
sources.license: Web runtime MIT; editor is a hosted product
sources.bestFor: Interactive vector animation driven by state machines
sources.caveat: Needs .riv files made in the Rive editor, so no local study here. Name the state machine explicitly in code.

sources.name: Unicorn Studio
sources.license: Commercial; the free plan prohibits commercial use
sources.bestFor: Designer-built shader heroes and effects without writing GLSL
sources.caveat: Scenes live in an account, so no local study here. Check plan terms before client work.

sources.name: Lucide
sources.framework: SVG icons, packages for most frameworks
sources.bestFor: The default stroke icon set for product UI
sources.caveat: One stroke style; use Phosphor when you need weights.

sources.name: Phosphor Icons
sources.bestFor: Icons in six weights (thin to duotone) for expressive interfaces
sources.caveat: Pick one weight per interface.

sources.name: Recent (formerly Godly)
sources.bestFor: Current, ambitious web design examples
sources.caveat: godly.website redirects here. Look, do not copy.

sources.name: Mobbin
sources.bestFor: Real app flows: onboarding, settings, checkout, paywalls
sources.caveat: Paid tiers; screenshots belong to the apps shown.

sources.name: Refero
sources.bestFor: Searchable web app screens and components
sources.caveat: Paid tiers.

sources.name: Land-book
sources.bestFor: Curated landing pages by industry and style
sources.caveat: Look, do not copy.

sources.name: Observable Plot
sources.bestFor: Clear explanatory and exploratory charts in very little code
sources.caveat: Styling defaults are plain; apply your tokens and direct labels.

sources.name: D3
sources.bestFor: Bespoke charts, maps and diagrams with full control
sources.caveat: Low level; use Plot first for standard charts.

sources.name: reveal.js
sources.bestFor: Slide decks as web pages with notes, fragments and PDF export
sources.caveat: Default themes look dated; bring your own type and tokens.

sources.name: Satori
sources.bestFor: Generating Open Graph images per page at build or request time
sources.caveat: Supports a subset of CSS (flexbox only); fonts must be passed in.

sources.name: Tyler Hobbs: Flow Fields
sources.bestFor: Understanding and tuning flow-field generative art
sources.caveat: Technique reference; the artworks are the artist's.

sources.name: Stencil Wiki: Riso ink colours
sources.bestFor: Screen approximations (hex) of real Riso inks for two- and three-colour designs
sources.caveat: Hex values are approximate; ask your printer which inks they stock.

styles.name: Liquid glass
styles.description: Glass that bends what is behind it.
styles.use: One floating control over rich imagery
styles.watch: Refraction is Chromium-only in CSS; keep text short and high-contrast.

styles.name: Dithering
styles.description: Two inks, ordered dots, retro-tech texture.
styles.use: Developer and AI brand moments, heroes

styles.name: Material expressive
styles.description: Shapes that change with state, springy motion.
styles.watch: Seed colours from the brand, not Material's baseline violet.

styles.name: Typographic poster
styles.description: Grid, scale and one colour do all the work.
styles.watch: Export text as outlines or ship the font.

styles.name: Risograph
styles.description: Flat inks that multiply, drift and grain.
styles.watch: Build per ink layer so it can really be printed.

styles.name: Generative art
styles.description: Seeded systems that draw unique artworks.
styles.watch: Palette and density decide quality; store the seed.

styles.name: Data graphics
styles.description: Charts that make one point clearly.
styles.watch: Title states the finding; direct labels; one highlight colour.

demos.title: Liquid glass lens
demos.summary: A draggable glass toolbar bends the stripes and type behind it.
demos.watch: Refraction renders in Chromium; other browsers get frosted glass.

demos.title: Ordered dither
demos.summary: A lit sphere drawn in two inks with a Bayer matrix.
demos.watch: Canvas 2D at low resolution; Paper Shaders has a production Dithering shader.

demos.title: Expressive controls
demos.summary: Buttons and segments that change shape as you press and pick.

demos.title: Variable-weight headline
demos.summary: Letters thicken as the pointer comes near.
demos.use: One hero word on portfolios and launches
demos.watch: One short word; needs a variable font with a wght axis.

demos.title: Grain gradient
demos.summary: Soft mesh colour with film grain, exported as SVG.
demos.watch: Grain prevents banding; keep text on a solid layer.

demos.title: Contrast-first colour scale
demos.summary: Ten steps solved to exact contrast targets from one hue.
demos.use: Accessible design tokens for any medium
demos.watch: WCAG 2 ratios; copy the generated CSS variables.

demos.title: Swiss event poster
demos.summary: An A-ratio poster on a 6×8 grid with three compositions.
demos.watch: Toggle the grid to see how everything snaps.

demos.title: Two-ink riso poster
demos.summary: Fluorescent inks overlap, drift and pick up paper grain.

demos.title: Flow field artwork
demos.summary: Seeded curves follow a noise field in a limited palette.
demos.watch: Store the seed to reproduce a piece.

demos.title: Truchet pattern
demos.summary: Rotated tiles join into continuous woven paths.
demos.watch: Stroke about a sixth of the tile size.

demos.title: Annotated line chart
demos.summary: The title states the finding; one line is highlighted and labelled.
demos.watch: Illustrative data; direct labels instead of a legend.
